comments.body:
**Claude finished @UBayouski's task in 31s** —— [View job](https://github.com/UBayouski/tracenotes/actions/runs/42270138300)

---
### Qodo finding: indented merge commits

- [x] Read `src/group.ts` and `src/commit.ts`
- [x] Decide whether the finding is valid
- [x] Add a test and run `npm run check` (67/67 pass)
- [x] Push to the branch

**I did not change `src/group.ts`. I think the finding is wrong, so I added a test that pins the current behavior.** Please overrule me if you disagree.

- **Why the finding is wrong:** `groupCommits` checks `message.raw.startsWith('Merge ')` on purpose, and the comment on that line says so. This follows AGENTS.md rule 6, Validate Before You Normalize. `parseCommit` trims the header only to build `subject`. Using that trimmed subject to spot merges would let `"  Merge branch x"` pass as a merge after whitespace was stripped, which is the mistake rule 6 forbids. Git writes merge subjects without leading spaces, so an indented one isn't a real merge.
- **Nothing is lost:** the commit lands in `Unclassified` with its SHA, so rules 1 and 2 (No Orphan Notes, Nothing Vanishes) still hold.
- **The test:** `rule 6: an indented "Merge " header is not a merge commit` in `tests/group.test.ts`. It asserts that `"  Merge branch x"` is not in `ignored`, appears under `Unclassified`, and `total === 1`. Commit `49c8632`.

If you would rather treat indented merges as ignored, that's a rule 6 change. It needs a documented exception in AGENTS.md first.
